subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add a core sub-agent `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` lifecycle contract, and what consumer-visible semantics should that contract guarantee?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but the proposed fix creates a new core event surface that affects gateway waits, persisted session state, SDK event normalization, and subagent completion behavior; automation should not choose that API contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt the additive lifecycle contract
options.body: Add `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` on current main, with explicit consumer behavior and regression proof across embedded-agent, registry, gateway, session, SDK, and docs.

options.title: Use existing diagnostics without new phases
options.body: Keep lifecycle phases unchanged and solve the hang through watchdog/session diagnostics and clearer timeout/abort projection, avoiding a new event contract but leaving less precise startup state.

options.title: Defer until sandbox-specific proof lands
options.body: Block the contract decision on the sandboxed subagent startup issue so the API is shaped around a live Docker failure case, at the cost of keeping this broader lifecycle gap open longer.

recommendation.title: Adopt the additive lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Add `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` on current main, with explicit consumer behavior and regression proof across embedded-agent, registry, gateway, session, SDK, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest available history across subagent lifecycle and the current agent/gateway surfaces affected by the decision.
